items.label: Northern Luzon
items.statement: A current Avibase taxonomic concept places the Yellow-crowned Flowerpecker in montane forest of Luzon.
items.source: Avibase bird taxonomic concept, Dicaeum anthonyi (McGregor 1914), source referencing original Philippine Journal of Science description
items.sourceLocation: Original description, name and type locality; Avibase current taxonomic concept
items.scopeLimit: The 1914 type locality and current taxonomic concept refer to Luzon birds, not the separately recognized Mindanao D. kampalili.

items.label: Montane forest
items.statement: Published species concepts associate the Luzon flowerpecker with tropical moist montane forest.
items.source: Avibase bird taxonomic concept, Dicaeum anthonyi (McGregor 1914), source referencing original Philippine Journal of Science description
items.sourceLocation: Original description, name and type locality; Avibase current taxonomic concept
items.scopeLimit: Habitat comes from a curated taxonomic reference, not a new peer-reviewed habitat survey.

items.label: Original type locality
items.statement: The original description cites Polls Mountain in Ifugao, Luzon, at approximately 2,000 m.
items.source: Avibase bird taxonomic concept, Dicaeum anthonyi (McGregor 1914), source referencing original Philippine Journal of Science description
items.sourceLocation: Original description, name and type locality; Avibase current taxonomic concept
items.scopeLimit: An original type locality is one historical site, not the full elevation range.

items.label: Distinction from Mindanao relative
items.statement: The Luzon population is treated as D. anthonyi and the Mindanao Flame-crowned Flowerpecker as D. kampalili.
items.source: Avibase bird taxonomic concept, Dicaeum anthonyi (McGregor 1914), source referencing original Philippine Journal of Science description
items.sourceLocation: Original description, name and type locality; Avibase current taxonomic concept
items.scopeLimit: Taxonomic splitting changes how older reports under D. anthonyi should be interpreted.

items.label: Morphological differentiation
items.statement: The 2008 original description distinguishes this Mindoro fruit bat from its relatives through external measurements, skull and dental morphology.
items.source: Esselstyn, Garcia, Saulog & Heaney (2008), Journal of Mammalogy 89:815–825
items.sourceLocation: Original diagnosis, type series, geographic and genetic comparison
items.scopeLimit: The publication uses multiple comparative characters, not a single photo-based diagnosis.

items.label: Closest named relative
items.statement: The original description compares the Mindoro taxon with D. leucopterus and supports its distinct status with mitochondrial sequence data.
items.source: Esselstyn, Garcia, Saulog & Heaney (2008), Journal of Mammalogy 89:815–825
items.sourceLocation: Original diagnosis, type series, geographic and genetic comparison
items.scopeLimit: Phylogenetic evidence is part of the published diagnosis.

items.label: Original Mindoro collection areas
items.statement: The original type series includes Mt. Siburan in western Mindoro and Mt. Halcon in eastern Mindoro.
items.source: Esselstyn, Garcia, Saulog & Heaney (2008), Journal of Mammalogy 89:815–825
items.sourceLocation: Original diagnosis, type series, geographic and genetic comparison
items.scopeLimit: The paper reports two sampled areas, not an island-wide census.

items.label: Study forest
items.statement: The original study recorded the species in secondary and primary forest on Mindoro.
items.source: Esselstyn, Garcia, Saulog & Heaney (2008), Journal of Mammalogy 89:815–825
items.sourceLocation: Original diagnosis, type series, geographic and genetic comparison
items.scopeLimit: Forest statements refer to original known localities.

items.label: Accepted name
items.statement: The ASM Mammal Diversity Database uses Desmalopex microleucoptera; the original description used D. microleucopterus.
items.source: ASM Mammal Diversity Database v2.5, Desmalopex microleucoptera taxon record (2026)
items.sourceLocation: Accepted taxon combination and original description citation
items.scopeLimit: Species epithet spelling was revised to agree with the feminine genus name.

items.label: 2018 global assessment
items.statement: The IUCN Red List assessed this species as Endangered under B1ab(iii,v) on 31 August 2018.
items.source: IUCN Red List, Desmalopex microleucopterus, assessed 31 August 2018; published 2019
items.sourceLocation: 2018 assessment B1ab(iii,v), elevation and range sections
items.scopeLimit: Global IUCN status in the cited 2019 publication, not a Philippine DENR legal category.

items.label: Global population trend
items.statement: The 2018 IUCN assessment reports a decreasing population trend.
items.source: IUCN Red List, Desmalopex microleucopterus, assessed 31 August 2018; published 2019
items.sourceLocation: 2018 assessment B1ab(iii,v), elevation and range sections
items.scopeLimit: The assessment is dated and does not quantify the current number of mature individuals.
